subject: reactive behaviour when coming from Javascript

messages.author: 9349b31ec7c243b2
messages.subject: reactive behaviour when coming from Javascript
parts:
Hello -

I get a variable from jQuery / Javascript that gives me the latitude and longitude of data that I would like to cause a reactive R script to run. How can I do that?

function updateLatitude(lat) {
$("input#lat").val(Math.round(lat));
}
<input type="number" id="lat" value="" name="lat" />

Thanks,
Dawg

messages.author: c6ca7877bef91eef
messages.subject: Re: reactive behaviour when coming from Javascript
parts:
Here is one approach (untested). Shiny uses the id element to identify an input. So in your case it will be input$lat. 

You can define a reactive function

data <- reactive(function(){
  input$dat
})

You can now call it inside the R function which you want to run, whenever this value gets updated

foo <- reactive(function(){
  data()
})

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: reactive behaviour when coming from Javascript
parts:
You don't need/want it to also be in a reactive function. Your R code was correct as written.

Are you seeing the number being correctly updated in the UI, and it's just not causing the R code to execute? If so, try this:

function updateLatitude(lat) {
$("input#lat").val(Math.round(lat));
$("input#lat").trigger("change");

}
<input type="number" id="lat" value="" name="lat" />
